newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechnya removes security chief - Russian agencies.
newsitem.headline: Chechnya removes security chief - Russian agencies.

text.p: Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov, plagued by a series of kidnappings, removed the head of the rebel Russian region's security service on Saturday, Russian news agencies said.

Interfax, RIA and Itar-Tass news agencies said Maskhadov had issued a decree replacing Abu Movsayev with his deputy, former separatist guerrilla commander Anti Batalov. It gave no reason for the decision.
Tass quoted Chechen Vice President Vakha Arsanov as saying by telephone that Movsayev had asked to be removed.

Russian media had said Movsayev tendered his resignation earlier this month on the same day as deputy prime minister Shamil Basayev quit, but later withdrew it. Movsayev had said at the time that he was tired.

Movsayev signed a provisional cooperation treaty only on Tuesday with Nikolai Kovalyov, head of Russia's Federal Security Service. It called for cooperation in fighting crimes such as kidnapping and arms and drug trading.

Hostage-taking has become a huge problem in Chechnya, where Russian troops fought separatist forces for 21 months until last August. Two Britons, one Frenchman and a Slovak were kidnapped this month in and around Chechnya.

Chechen authorities say their region in the north Caucasus is independent from Russia. Moscow has ruled out full independence but has put off solving the sovereignty issue for five years under a peace treaty with Chechnya.
